subject: DPA: data residency + backup/recovery retention exception — clarification request
messages:
From: Mike Tucker <mike.tucker@acme.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA: backup/restore retention & certified erase — quick clarification

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Legal asked me to follow up with a few narrow clarifications so they can sign off on the DPA:

1) Backup / recovery snapshots: we need to understand the maximum retention window for backups/snapshots that contain customer data. Our procurement team is seeing language that says "backups may be retained for operational recovery" but there's no explicit maximum period. Can you confirm Redwood's typical max retention period for backups that could contain customer data and whether that can be capped in the DPA?

2) Incident recovery exception: in the event of a major outage (e.g., full region restore), are backups allowed to be retained for a longer period solely for recovery, and can we require documented justification and an automatic revert to normal retention once recovery is complete?

3) Certified erasure: if Acme requests erasure for a tenant, what is the end-to-end timeline for erasing data from backups and snapshots? Are we able to provide a certification (signed statement) when erasure is complete?

Attaching the SOC snapshot Legal referenced — happy to jump on a quick call if useful.

Thanks,

Mike Tucker
Head of Cloud Procurement — Acme Cloud

(415) 555-0199

Subject: Re: DPA: backup/restore retention & certified erase — quick clarification

Hi Mike —

Thanks, this is helpful and straightforward to address. Short answers up-front:
- Typical operational backups: 30–90 days depending on config; default platform behavior is 30 days for short-term snapshots, 90 days for disaster recovery artifacts.
- Incident recovery exception: yes, we can allow a temporary extension for recovery with documented justification, a timebox, and automatic reversion.
- Certified erasure: we can issue a signed erasure confirmation after the deletion workflow completes; timelines depend on whether a backup sweep is required (see below).

I'll loop in Karthik (infra) and Laura (legal ops) to propose firm redline language you can take to Acme Legal. I have two questions for you before I draft language:
1) Is Acme comfortable with a 30-day default and a 90-day disaster-recovery max, or would you prefer default=60 / max=180?
2) For the erasure certification, does Legal need a specific template or just a signed statement that lists the artifacts removed and the date range?

Happy to propose language in-line and attach a redline.

Best,

Priya Natarajan
Head of Security & Compliance Partnerships
Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Jul 2028 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: DPA: backup/restore retention & certified erase — proposed redlines

Karthik / Laura — forwarding Acme's questions (below). I drafted suggested DPA redlines and an incident retention matrix for operational review. See attachments: redlined_DPA_v3.docx and incident_retention_matrix.xlsx. High-level proposal follows — please review and comment inline, I want technical validation from Karthik and a legal ops sanity check from Laura before we send to Mike.

Draft redline bullets (short):
- Backup retention (default): "Redwood will retain automated short-term snapshots for 30 days by default. Disaster recovery snapshots may be retained for up to 90 days following creation for the sole purpose of service restoration."
- Incident recovery extension: "In the event of a documented incident requiring extended retention for recovery, Redwood may retain relevant backups for a further time-limited period not to exceed 90 days beyond the standard retention. Redwood will provide Acme with written justification and a recovery completion date; retained artifacts will be purged automatically no later than that date unless otherwise agreed in writing."
- Certified erasure: "Upon Acme's verified request to erase Acme tenant data, Redwood will: (a) perform live-tenant data deletion within 30 days; (b) perform backup/snapshot sweep to remove identified Acme data from retained artifacts within 90 days of the erasure request; (c) provide a signed erasure certificate confirming the actions taken and listing artifacts removed."
- Lawful hold carveout: "Redwood may suspend purge obligations for specific artifacts subject to lawful hold or legal process, provided Redwood notifies Acme and maintains audit logs of retained items."

Questions for Karthik (tech):
- Can you confirm the 90-day sweep for backups is operationally realistic and whether we should add language about "best effort" vs guaranteed?
- Are there any SKUs or archive flows we need to call out separately (cold storage snapshots, cross-region replicas)?

Laura — from an ops/legal perspective, is the phrasing above sufficient for procurement or do you want a shorter SLA-style clause?

Thanks — Priya

Attachment stubs: redlined_DPA_v3.docx, incident_retention_matrix.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 Jul 2028 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA: backup/restore retention & certified erase — proposed redlines

Priya — quick tech validation and suggested tweaks below. Quoting Mike's initial asks for context.

Operational notes:
- 30-day default for auto-snapshots is safe and already in production for most customers.
- 90-day DR snapshot max is feasible, but we should make it explicit that DR snapshots are tagged and segregated and that retention beyond default requires a formal "Recovery Justification" ticket. That ticket should include the affected time range and an expected completion date.
- Backup sweep: a full sweep that guarantees removal from all media (including cold replicas) within 90 days is operationally expensive but doable for customers who have an enterprise SLA and commit to an evidence retrieval window. For standard customers, we can commit to "logical removal" within 30 days and a physical media reclamation within 90 days. Suggest two-tier language: "logical deletion" (30d) + "physical purge completion" (90d).
- Cross-region replicas: call these out. If replicas exist in a non-Acme region, we need to specify geofencing behavior or confirm there's no cross-border copy. If customer requires strict residency, we must add residency-specific handling for replicas.

Suggested revised redline sentence (short):
"Redwood will logically delete tenant data from live production stores within 30 days of a validated erasure request. For backups and replicated artifacts, Redwood will: (i) perform logical exclusion/suppression of the tenant's data within 30 days; and (ii) complete physical media reclamation and removal of the tenant's data artifacts within 90 days, unless subject to lawful hold. Recovery-only retention beyond standard retention windows requires a documented Recovery Justification ticket and will be limited to an additional 90 days unless otherwise agreed."

I'll drop comments directly into redlined_DPA_v3.docx and link the internal playbook here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cACME-retention-matrix

Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Priya / Karthik —

Thanks for the clear options and the redline. Acme Legal reviewed and we are comfortable with the two-tier logical/physical approach, with two small changes to propose back to Redwood:

1) Default retention: please move the platform default to 60 days for short-term snapshots instead of 30 days — Acme operations relies on a slightly longer window for nearline restores.
2) Recovery extension cap: we'd like the maximum recovery extension to be 60 days beyond standard retention (instead of 90) unless there's a documented executive exception process.

If Redwood accepts those two edits, Legal is ready to sign the revised DPA. Please upload the updated redline to DocuSign and send the link for signature.
